q: API Gateway 在微服务架构里的核心定位是什么？
q_en: What is the core role of an API Gateway in a microservice architecture?
options: 只做负载均衡，不涉及路由或协议转换
把所有业务逻辑塞进网关，取代后端服务
统一入口，把请求路由到合适的后端服务
给服务间异步通信用的消息队列
options_en: Just a load balancer, with no routing or protocol translation
Putting all business logic into the gateway, replacing backend services
A single entry point that routes requests to the right backend service
A message queue for asynchronous service-to-service communication
why: API Gateway 的核心定位是入口 + 路由：把客户端和内部服务拓扑隔开。它不是纯负载均衡器，也不该承接业务逻辑。
why_en: An API Gateway is the client-facing entry point that routes requests to backend services, not a pure load balancer or a home for business logic.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Client[Client] --> Gateway[API Gateway]
  Gateway --> User[User service]
  Gateway --> Order[Order service]
  Gateway --> Pay[Payment service]
optionExplanations: 负载均衡只管流量分发，没有路由表和协议转换能力，覆盖不了网关全部职责。
把业务逻辑塞进网关会让网关代码膨胀、越权代管后端职责，等于白拆了微服务。
网关是客户端与后端服务之间的统一入口，按路径、方法等把请求送到对应服务。
消息队列服务异步事件传递，不负责同步请求该走哪个服务这种路由判断。
optionExplanations_en: A load balancer alone only splits traffic, with no routing table or protocol translation, so it can't cover a gateway's full job.
Stuffing business logic into the gateway bloats it and takes over backend duties, undoing the point of splitting services.
The gateway sits between clients and services as one entry point, forwarding each request onward by path or method.
Message queues carry asynchronous events; they don't make the synchronous call of which service handles a request.

q: 面试中提到 API Gateway 时，最容易漏掉但最核心的职责是？
q_en: When you mention an API Gateway in an interview, what core responsibility is easiest to miss?
options: 缓存所有用户私有响应
替代 Kafka 做事件流处理
请求路由：判断每个请求该交给哪个后端服务
直接执行 SQL 查询并返回结果
options_en: Caching every user-private response
Replacing Kafka for event stream processing
Request routing: deciding which backend service handles each request
Directly executing SQL queries and returning results
why: 很多候选人只讲认证、限流等 middleware，却漏掉 gateway 存在的根本理由——请求路由。middleware 是常见附加能力，不该盖过它。
why_en: The gateway’s primary responsibility is request routing, while authentication and rate limiting are secondary middleware.
optionExplanations: 缓存用户私有响应有跨用户泄露的风险，也不是网关最容易被漏讲的核心职责。
事件流是独立的异步系统，网关不会去顶替 Kafka 处理这类持久化订阅。
把每个请求分发给该处理它的服务，是网关存在的根本原因，比认证限流更基础。
直接跑 SQL 属于后端服务的职责，网关一旦这么做就侵入了数据层。
optionExplanations_en: Caching private per-user responses risks leaking data across users, and it isn't the duty candidates usually forget.
Event streaming is a separate persistent async system; a gateway doesn't stand in for something like Kafka.
Deciding which service handles each request is the reason a gateway exists at all, more basic than auth or limits.
Running SQL directly belongs to a backend service; a gateway doing that reaches straight into the data layer.

q: 哪些属于 API Gateway 常见的 middleware / cross-cutting concern？
q_en: Which items are common API Gateway middleware or cross-cutting concerns?
options: JWT 认证
请求限流
CORS 处理
训练推荐模型
options_en: JWT authentication
Rate limiting
Handling CORS
Training a recommendation model
why: API Gateway 常处理认证、限流、SSL、CORS 等跨服务通用逻辑，因为每个服务重复实现这些逻辑会造成大量重复代码。
why_en: Gateways centralize cross-cutting middleware such as authentication, rate limiting, and CORS handling to avoid duplicating them per service.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Request[Request] --> Auth[JWT auth]
  Auth --> Limit[Rate limit]
  Limit --> CORS[CORS]
  CORS --> Route[Route to service]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自包含的令牌格式，把身份和权限声明编码进去，放在请求头里传递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JWT stands for JSON Web Token, a self-contained token that encodes identity claims and travels in the request header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器跨域请求时，服务端要用特定响应头显式允许的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CORS stands for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, the header-based mechanism that lets a browser call an API on a different origin.

optionExplanations: JWT 认证挡住未携带有效身份令牌的请求，避免每个服务各自重复校验身份。
请求限流挡住突发流量把某个后端打垮的风险，在入口就先削峰。
CORS 处理省掉每个服务各自加跨域响应头的重复劳动，统一在网关搞定。
训练推荐模型是离线 ML 流水线的工作，不会出现在同步请求的入口路径上。
optionExplanations_en: JWT auth blocks requests without a valid identity token, so no single service has to re-check identity on its own.
Rate limiting blocks a traffic burst from taking down a backend, shaving the peak right at the entry point.
Handling CORS at the gateway saves every service from adding its own cross-origin headers.
Training a recommendation model is offline pipeline work; it never sits on a synchronous request's entry path.

q: 把一次经过 API Gateway 的请求按合理顺序排列：
q_en: Put a request through an API Gateway in the usual order.
steps: 后端服务处理请求并返回结果
Gateway 可选地缓存可复用响应
Gateway 根据路由规则选择后端服务
Gateway 执行认证、限流等 middleware
Gateway 转换响应并返回给客户端
why: 典型流程先挡掉无效请求，再应用通用策略，然后路由到服务，最后转换响应并可选缓存；这个顺序解释了网关在链路上的位置。
why_en: A typical gateway flow validates, applies middleware, routes, waits for the backend response, transforms it, and optionally caches it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> Validate[Validate request]
Validate --> Middleware[Auth / rate limit]
Middleware --> Route[Route to service]
Route --> Service[Backend service]
Service --> Transform[Transform response]
Transform --> Cache[Optional cache]
Cache --> Client

q: 为什么 API Gateway 通常要在路由前做请求校验？
q_en: Why does an API Gateway usually validate a request before routing it?
options: 尽早拒绝缺 header 或缺 API key 的无效请求
跳过入口所有校验，直接把请求原样转发给后端处理
无条件把每一个请求都写入数据库做审计留痕
彻底跳过身份认证服务，只保留限流这一层逻辑
options_en: Reject requests early that are missing headers or an API key
Skip all entry-layer validation and forward the request to the backend exactly as received
Unconditionally write every single request to a database purely for audit purposes
Skip identity authentication entirely and keep only the rate-limiting logic
why: 早期校验能省掉后端对无效请求的计算和 I/O，并返回更清晰的错误；它专门挑格式、header、body schema、API key 这类入口级问题。
why_en: Early validation rejects malformed or incomplete requests before they consume backend compute and I/O.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端在请求头或参数里携带的字符串凭证，用来标识调用方身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a string credential a client sends so the gateway can identify who is calling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端与 Gateway 之间最常见的应用层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol clients typically use to talk to a gateway.

optionExplanations: 格式或凭证缺失的请求在入口就被拦下，后端不用再为它花计算和 I/O。
不做入口检查会让无效请求一路打到后端才失败，浪费的资源反而更多。
把校验换成数据库审计写入，既没做格式检查，还多了一次写入开销。
去掉认证只留限流，限流不知道调用方是谁，容易被绕过。
optionExplanations_en: A request missing headers or an API key gets turned away at the door, before it costs the backend any compute or I/O.
Skipping entry checks lets an invalid request travel all the way to the backend before it fails, wasting more resources.
Swapping validation for a database audit write skips the format check entirely and adds an extra write.
Dropping auth and keeping only rate limiting leaves no way to know who's calling, so limits are easy to dodge.

q: 补全 API Gateway 的核心路由依据：
q_en: Fill in the main inputs an API Gateway can use for routing.
text: Gateway 的 routing table 通常可以根据 {{URL path}}、{{HTTP method}}、{{query parameters}} 和 {{request headers}} 把请求映射到后端服务。
why: 路径是最常见的路由依据，但方法、查询参数和 header 也能参与路由，比如 /users/* 走 user-service、/payments/* 走 payment-service。
why_en: Gateway routing can key off the URL path, HTTP method, query parameters, and request headers to pick the backend service.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识请求资源位置的地址，是 Gateway 路由匹配的主要依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address a gateway’s routing table matches against.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端与 Gateway 之间最常见的应用层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol clients typically use to talk to a gateway.

scenario: 你的系统拆成 user-service、order-service、payment-service，移动端不应该知道每个服务的地址和端口。
scenario_en: Your backend is split into user-service, order-service, and payment-service, and the mobile app should not know each service address or port.
q: 入口层最适合加什么组件？
q_en: What component best fits the entry layer?
options: 把所有服务地址都硬编码进移动端代码里
只加一个离线数据仓库
API Gateway，按路由规则转发到对应服务
让每个服务直接暴露公网端口
options_en: Hardcode every service address directly into the mobile app's codebase
Just add an offline data warehouse
An API Gateway that forwards by routing rules
Let every service expose its own public port
why: 微服务场景下，Gateway 给客户端一个稳定入口并隐藏内部拓扑；服务拆分、迁移或扩容时客户端不需要跟着改。
why_en: A gateway fits microservices because it gives clients one stable endpoint while hiding internal service topology.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统只有一个简单 monolith 或一个后端服务，直接 client-server 通信通常更简单。
tradeoff: 统一入口隐藏拓扑 vs 客户端直连更简单但强耦合
optionExplanations: 把地址写死在客户端的做法几乎撑不住——服务一拆分或迁移，就得逼所有用户升级 App。
离线数据仓库跑批处理任务，不接实时客户端请求，解决不了入口这个问题。
后端拆成多个服务、客户端不该感知内部拓扑时，统一入口最合适。
每个服务各开公网端口，只在完全不需要隐藏内部结构时才说得通，这里正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Hardcoding addresses only works if services never move; split or migrate one and every client needs a forced update.
An offline warehouse handles batch jobs, not live client traffic, so it doesn't solve the entry-point problem here.
When the backend splits into several services and clients shouldn't see the internal layout, one stable entry fits.
Exposing every service on its own public port only makes sense if you don't need to hide topology, the opposite here.

q: 在“是否值得引入 API Gateway”这个维度上，哪种判断更合理？
q_en: What is the right way to decide whether adding an API Gateway is worth it?
options: 任何系统都必须引入 API Gateway
只有离线批处理系统才需要 API Gateway
微服务外部入口通常适合；简单单体架构可能过度设计
只要用了 PostgreSQL 就必须加 Gateway
options_en: Every system must add an API Gateway
A gateway is only useful for offline batch systems
It fits microservice entry points but can be overkill for a simple monolith
Using PostgreSQL automatically requires a gateway
why: Gateway 的收益来自隐藏多个后端服务和集中入口策略；内部结构简单时它只会增加部署和调试复杂度。
why_en: A gateway is most useful for microservices and can be unnecessary complexity for a simple monolith.
tradeoff: 微服务需要统一入口 vs 简单单体多背一层复杂度
optionExplanations: 把网关说成任何系统的硬性要求，忽略了单体架构根本用不上它的事实。
离线批处理不面向同步入口请求，网关的适用范围恰恰说反了。
拆成多服务时统一入口收益明显，单体只多背一层部署和调试成本。
数据库选型和是否需要网关是两个独立决策，PostgreSQL 不会触发这个前提。
optionExplanations_en: Calling it mandatory for every system ignores that a monolith has no real use for one.
Offline batch systems never face synchronous entry traffic, so this gets the fit backwards.
Splitting into services makes a shared entry point pay off; a monolith just carries the extra deploy and debug cost.
Database choice and needing a gateway are unrelated decisions; PostgreSQL alone doesn't trigger this.

q: 面试里最常被认为有实际价值的 API Gateway middleware 是哪些？
q_en: Which API Gateway middleware is usually worth mentioning in interviews?
options: 认证
限流
IP allowlist/blocklist
训练搜索排序模型
options_en: Authentication
Rate limiting
IP allowlist/blocklist
Training a search ranking model
why: 认证、限流和 IP 名单都是入口层通用策略，放在 Gateway 能避免每个服务重复实现；排序模型训练不属于入口职责。
why_en: Authentication, rate limiting, and IP allow/block lists are the gateway middleware interviewers expect to hear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，Gateway 常用源 IP 做 allow/block 名单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP stands for Internet Protocol, and gateways often allow or block traffic by source IP address.

optionExplanations: 认证挡住没有合法身份的调用方，放网关能一次保护所有后端服务。
限流挡住突发流量拖垮后端的风险，统一在入口就能全局生效。
IP allowlist/blocklist 挡住来自已知恶意或未授权网段的请求。
排序模型训练是离线流程，不产生任何入口该拦截或放行的实时判断。
optionExplanations_en: Auth blocks callers without valid identity, protecting every backend service from one place.
Rate limiting blocks a traffic spike from overwhelming the backend, enforced once at the entry point.
An IP allow/block list blocks traffic from known-bad or unauthorized network ranges.
Ranking-model training is offline work; it makes no real-time allow-or-block call at the entry.

scenario: 某 GET endpoint 对相同输入总返回同样的公开结果，访问频率很高，数据变化不频繁。
scenario_en: A GET endpoint returns the same public result for the same input, gets heavy traffic, and changes infrequently.
q: API Gateway 可以怎么优化？
q_en: How can the API Gateway optimize this endpoint?
options: 强制每一次请求都直接穿透到最深层的数据库查询里
不管请求内容，随机返回一个缓存值
要求客户端跳过网关直连数据库
在 Gateway 层缓存响应，用 TTL 或事件失效
options_en: Force every single request to punch straight through to the deepest database query
Ignore the request content and return a random cached value
Have clients skip the gateway and connect to the database directly
Cache the response at the gateway with TTL or event-based invalidation
why: 对非用户私有、输入相同输出稳定的结果，Gateway 缓存能减少后端负载和延迟，用 TTL 或事件触发失效即可。
why_en: Gateway caching fits public deterministic responses where the same input always returns the same output.
whenOtherWins: 如果响应强依赖用户身份、权限或实时状态，缓存要更谨慎，甚至不该放在 Gateway。
tradeoff: 命中缓存降低后端负载 vs 私有/实时数据不能这样缓存
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Client[Client] --> Gateway[Gateway]
  Gateway --> Hit{Cache hit?}
  Hit -->|yes| Cached[Return cached response]
  Hit -->|no| Service[Backend service]
  Service --> Store[Store with TTL]
  Store --> Client
  Cached --> Client

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，过期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL stands for Time To Live, the duration a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 每次都打穿到数据库，白白浪费了这个 endpoint 输出稳定、可复用的前提。
缓存的前提是相同输入给相同输出，随机返回值直接破坏了正确性。
让客户端绕开网关直连数据库，暴露内部实现，也丢了入口层的统一控制。
响应公开且确定，用 TTL 或事件失效在网关缓存，能实打实降负载降延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Punching through to the database every time wastes the fact that this endpoint's output is stable and reusable.
Caching assumes same input gives same output; returning an arbitrary value breaks correctness outright.
Having clients bypass the gateway for the database exposes internals and gives up entry-layer control.
Public, deterministic output fits gateway caching with TTL or event-driven invalidation to cut load and latency.

q: Gateway 层缓存最不适合哪类响应？
q_en: Which response type is the worst fit for gateway-level caching?
options: 公开的配置列表
公共商品分类页
同输入稳定输出的静态数据
每个用户看到的私有账户信息
options_en: A public configuration list
A public product category page
Static data with the same output for the same input
Private account information unique to each user
why: 用户私有响应容易因权限、身份、实时状态不同而产生缓存污染或泄露；Gateway 缓存更适合公开、稳定、可复用的响应。
why_en: Gateway caching is risky for user-specific private responses because a shared cache entry can leak between users.
tradeoff: 公开稳定数据可缓存 vs 用户私有数据缓存有泄露风险
optionExplanations: 变更很少的公开配置命中率高、风险低，是缓存的舒适区。
商品分类结构稳定、人人看到一样，同样适合设置较长 TTL。
输入决定输出且不因人而异，是教科书式的可缓存场景。
权限和身份因人而异，缓存命中可能把 A 的数据错发给 B，风险最高。
optionExplanations_en: Public config that rarely changes gets a high hit rate with low risk, comfortable caching territory.
A product category page is stable and identical for every visitor, so a longer TTL fits fine too.
Output depends only on input and never on who's asking, the textbook case for caching.
Permissions and identity differ by who is asking, so a cache hit can hand user A's data to user B, the riskiest case here.

q: API Gateway 可能采用哪些缓存策略？
q_en: Which caching strategies can an API Gateway use?
options: 缓存整个响应
只缓存响应中变化少的一部分
TTL 或事件驱动失效
永远不允许任何缓存失效
options_en: Caching the entire response
Caching only the slow-changing part of a response
TTL or event-driven invalidation
Never allowing any cache to be invalidated
why: Gateway 可以做整份响应缓存、部分缓存，但都需要清晰的失效策略；没有失效机制的缓存会长期返回过期数据。
why_en: Gateway caching can store whole responses or stable fragments, but it always needs TTL or event-based invalidation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，过期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL stands for Time To Live, the duration a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 整份响应缓存实现最简单，能挡住重复请求重新算一遍的开销，代价是占内存。
只缓存变化少的片段，把压力从频繁计算里减掉，同时留出灵活刷新的空间。
TTL 或事件失效挡住缓存长期返回过期数据这个正确性风险，是缓存必须搭配的机制。
条目写入后永不过期，等于主动放弃了失效保护，迟早会返回错误数据。
optionExplanations_en: Caching the whole response is the simplest approach, blocking repeat requests from recomputing at the cost of memory.
Caching only the slow-changing part takes pressure off frequent computation while staying flexible to refresh.
TTL or event-driven invalidation blocks the risk of serving stale data forever, a mechanism caching must pair with.
Never letting an entry lapse gives up invalidation protection entirely, and stale data eventually leaks through.

scenario: 客户端只说 HTTP，但内部 user-service 用 gRPC 通信以获得更好的性能。
scenario_en: Clients only speak HTTP, but the internal user-service uses gRPC for better service-to-service performance.
q: API Gateway 在协议不一致时可以承担什么角色？
q_en: What role can an API Gateway play when client and internal protocols differ?
options: 强制要求所有内部服务全部改成浏览器脚本语言来写
直接删除掉服务之间的所有通信链路
协议转换：HTTP 请求转 gRPC，再转回客户端格式
只负责压缩前端的静态资源文件
options_en: Force every single internal service to be rewritten in a browser scripting language
Delete every communication path between the services outright
Protocol translation: turn the HTTP request into gRPC, then translate back
Only handle compression of frontend static asset files
why: Gateway 可以把外部 HTTP 面和内部高效协议隔离开，但这不是每个系统都要做——只有内外协议确实不同且收益明确时才需要。
why_en: A gateway can translate between client-facing HTTP and an internal protocol like gRPC when the two genuinely differ.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端与 Gateway 之间最常见的应用层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol clients typically use to talk to a gateway.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种高效的二进制 RPC 协议，常用于服务间的内部通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC stands for gRPC Remote Procedure Call, a binary RPC protocol often used for internal service-to-service calls.

optionExplanations: 把内部服务全改成浏览器脚本语言是不现实的大规模重写，也没解决协议不一致本身。
删掉服务间通信链路，协作直接崩掉，问题不是变小而是变得没法用。
网关做协议转换，外部保持 HTTP、内部继续用高效的 gRPC，两边互不干扰。
静态资源压缩和协议是否一致完全是两回事，解决不了 HTTP/gRPC 的落差。
optionExplanations_en: Rewriting every internal service into a browser scripting language is an unrealistic overhaul that doesn't touch the protocol gap.
Deleting the communication paths breaks service collaboration outright, that's removing the problem, not solving it.
The gateway translates protocols: external traffic stays HTTP while internal calls keep using efficient gRPC underneath.
Compressing static frontend assets has nothing to do with whether HTTP and gRPC line up.

q: 补全 Gateway 响应转换的目标：
q_en: Fill in the goal of response transformation at the gateway.
text: 后端服务可以使用内部最合适的协议或格式，API Gateway 再把响应转换成客户端需要的 {{clean}}、{{consistent}} API 格式。
why: 响应转换让内部实现和外部 API 解耦：内部 gRPC 响应可以被 Gateway 转成 HTTP JSON 返回给移动端。
why_en: Response transformation lets backend services keep their internal format while clients receive one clean, consistent API.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种高效的二进制 RPC 协议，常用于服务间的内部通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC stands for gRPC Remote Procedure Call, a binary RPC protocol often used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端与 Gateway 之间最常见的应用层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol clients typically use to talk to a gateway.

scenario: 入口请求量上升，但 API Gateway 实例不保存会话状态或业务状态。
scenario_en: Entry traffic is increasing, and the API Gateway instances do not store session state or business state.
q: 最直接的扩展方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most straightforward way to scale it?
options: 把所有请求固定打到一个 Gateway 实例
在负载均衡器后面水平增加多个 Gateway 实例
把 Gateway 改成单机有状态队列
让客户端随机访问数据库分片
options_en: Pin every request to a single gateway instance
Add more gateway instances horizontally behind a load balancer
Turn the gateway into a single stateful queue
Let clients randomly hit database shards
why: Gateway 通常无状态，因此可以横向扩容：前置 LB 把请求分发到多个 Gateway 实例即可。
why_en: A stateless gateway scales horizontally by adding instances behind a load balancer.
whenOtherWins: 如果 Gateway 持有本地会话或连接状态，就要先解决状态迁移或粘性会话，再谈扩容。
tradeoff: 无状态水平扩容 vs 有状态实例需要额外的会话管理
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Clients[Clients] --> LB[Load balancer]
  LB --> G1[Gateway instance]
  LB --> G2[Gateway instance]
  LB --> G3[Gateway instance]
  G1 --> Services[Backend services]
  G2 --> Services
  G3 --> Services
optionExplanations: 把流量钉死在一个实例上，恰恰是无状态组件本该避免的瓶颈。
实例不存业务状态时，LB 后面加实例就能线性分摊流量，随时增减。
把无状态的网关改成有状态队列，反而丢掉了随便加减实例的能力。
让客户端自己挑分片，等于把路由决策和分片细节甩给了客户端。
optionExplanations_en: Pinning all traffic to a single instance is exactly the bottleneck a stateless component should avoid.
With no business state in an instance, adding more behind the load balancer spreads traffic and scales freely.
Turning the stateless gateway into a stateful queue gives up the ability to add or remove instances at will.
Making clients pick their own shard hands routing decisions and shard details over to the client.

q: Client-to-Gateway LB 和 Gateway-to-Service LB 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between client-to-gateway load balancing and gateway-to-service load balancing?
options: 前者由入口 LB 处理；后者由 Gateway 做后端间分发
两者都只能交给数据库来完成负载均衡
前者其实只用于离线批处理，后者则只用于静态资源分发
两者完全相同，架构图里永远要画两个独立队列
options_en: The first is handled by a front LB; the second is the gateway balancing backends
Both can only be done by handing the job to a database
The first is actually only for offline batch jobs, the second only for static asset delivery
The two are identical and always need two separate queues in the diagram
why: 客户端到 Gateway 的流量一般先过 ELB/NGINX 等入口 LB；Gateway 再按服务发现和健康状态选择后端实例，是两层不同职责。
why_en: Client-to-gateway load balancing is handled by a front load balancer, while the gateway itself balances traffic across backend instances.
tradeoff: 入口负载均衡 vs 服务发现负载均衡，两层职责不同

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管负载均衡服务，常放在 Gateway 前面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ELB stands for Elastic Load Balancer, AWS’s managed load balancer often placed in front of a gateway.

optionExplanations: 两跳分别有不同的负责方：入口 LB 管客户端到网关，网关自己再管到后端实例。
数据库不参与流量分发决策，把均衡职责归给它完全说错了角色。
离线批处理和静态资源分发都跟这两层负载均衡没关系，场景判断错了。
两层用的判断数据和层级完全不同，说它们没区别忽视了这一点。
optionExplanations_en: The two hops have different owners: a front LB handles client-to-gateway, the gateway itself handles gateway-to-backend.
A database plays no role in traffic distribution, assigning it that job is simply the wrong component.
Neither offline batch jobs nor static asset delivery has anything to do with these two balancing layers.
The two hops decide on different data at different layers, calling them identical misses that.

scenario: 用户分布在多个大洲，入口 API 延迟明显，且服务已经有多 region 部署计划。
scenario_en: Users are spread across continents, entry API latency is noticeable, and the services already have a multi-region deployment plan.
q: API Gateway 层可以怎么设计？
q_en: How should the API Gateway layer be designed?
options: 只在一个遥远的 region 部署单个 Gateway
多区域部署，GeoDNS 路由到最近入口
直接删除掉所有已配置的路由规则
让客户端自己扫描发现所有 region
options_en: Deploy a single gateway in only one distant region
Deploy multi-region gateways with GeoDNS routing to the nearest one
Delete every routing rule that has been configured
Make clients scan and discover every region themselves
why: 全球用户场景可以把 Gateway 部署得更靠近用户，类似 CDN 的入口思路；关键风险是各区域路由规则要保持一致。
why_en: For global users, gateways can be deployed regionally with GeoDNS routing and synchronized configuration.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户集中在单一区域，先做单 region Gateway 和普通水平扩容更简单。
tradeoff: 多区域降延迟 vs 配置同步带来的运维成本
diagram:
flowchart TD
  NA[NA users] --> DNS[GeoDNS]
  EU[EU users] --> DNS
  DNS --> USGW[US gateway]
  DNS --> EUGW[EU gateway]
  USGW --> USSvc[US services]
  EUGW --> EUSvc[EU services]
  Config[Synced config] --> USGW
  Config --> EUGW

termDefinitions.meaning: 按用户地理位置把域名解析到最近入口的 DNS 机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GeoDNS resolves a domain to the nearest regional gateway based on the user’s geographic location.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDN stands for Content Delivery Network, edge nodes that cache content close to users.

optionExplanations: 把入口固定在一个遥远 region，全球用户依旧要跨洲访问，延迟问题没解决。
用户遍布多大洲且服务已多区域部署时，就近入口配 GeoDNS 能实打实降低首跳延迟。
删光路由规则等于让入口机制彻底失效，请求连转发都做不到。
让客户端自己扫描发现 region，复杂度和出错概率都会暴涨。
optionExplanations_en: Pinning the entry point to one distant region still leaves every global user crossing continents, latency stays unsolved.
With users spread across continents and services already multi-region, nearby entry points plus GeoDNS cut first-hop latency for real.
Wiping out every routing rule kills the entry mechanism entirely, requests can't even be forwarded.
Making clients scan for regions themselves pushes complexity and misconfiguration risk onto the client.

q: 全球化部署 API Gateway 时通常要考虑哪些点？
q_en: What should you consider when deploying API Gateways globally?
options: 区域 Gateway 部署
GeoDNS 路由到较近区域
跨区域配置同步
强制所有用户访问同一个内存变量
options_en: Regional gateway deployments
GeoDNS routing to the nearest region
Cross-region configuration synchronization
Forcing every user to hit the same in-memory variable
why: 多 region Gateway 的难点不只是部署实例，还包括入口路由和策略一致性；配置漂移会导致不同地区行为不一致。
why_en: Global gateway deployments need regional instances, geo-aware routing, and synchronized configuration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按用户地理位置把域名解析到最近入口的 DNS 机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GeoDNS resolves a domain to the nearest regional gateway based on the user’s geographic location.

optionExplanations: 区域 Gateway 部署让每个地区用户都能就近接入，减少跨洲请求的距离。
GeoDNS 把请求解析到最近入口，把跨洲延迟这块压力从物理距离上减掉。
跨区域配置同步挡住了不同地区路由规则漂移、行为不一致的风险。
让全球请求共用一个进程内变量，在分布式部署下根本不可能实现。
optionExplanations_en: Regional gateway deployments let each region's users connect nearby, cutting the distance on cross-continent requests.
GeoDNS resolves requests to the nearest entry point, taking the pressure of cross-continent latency off distance.
Cross-region config sync blocks the risk of routing rules drifting apart and regions behaving inconsistently.
Sharing one in-process variable across every global request simply isn't possible in a distributed deployment.

q: 托管 API Gateway 与开源/自管方案的主要取舍是？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff between managed and self-managed API Gateway options?
options: 托管方案完全不能做限流，自管方案完全不能做路由
两种方案都只能用来做数据库备份
开源方案在任何场景下都比托管方案简单
托管省运维但成本高控制少；自管控制多但要自己运维
options_en: Managed cannot do rate limiting at all, self-managed cannot do routing at all
Both options are only useful for database backups
Open source is simpler than managed in every scenario
Managed saves ops but costs more and gives less control; self-managed gives more control but you run it yourself
why: AWS API Gateway、Azure API Management 等托管服务降低运维成本；Kong、Tyk 等给团队更多控制。选择取决于生态、成本和运维能力。
why_en: Managed gateways reduce operational burden at higher cost, while self-managed gateways trade more ops work for more control.
tradeoff: 托管省运维 vs 自管拿控制权

termDefinitions.meaning: 亚马逊的云平台，提供托管 API Gateway 产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS stands for Amazon Web Services, whose managed API Gateway integrates with Lambda and CloudWatch.

optionExplanations: 限流和路由两种方案其实都能做，说某一方完全做不到是编出来的能力缺口。
两种方案都不是拿来做数据库备份的，说法完全跑题。
开源是否更简单取决于团队运维能力，用绝对化说法替代了真实取舍。
托管省运维但控制少、成本高；自管拿到控制权但要自己扛运维，这才是真取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Both options can actually do rate limiting and routing; claiming either can't is an invented capability gap.
Neither option is for database backups, that's simply off-topic.
Whether open source is simpler depends on the team's ops capability, this swaps a real tradeoff for an absolute claim.
Managed cuts ops work but costs more and gives less control; self-managed hands back control at the price of running it yourself.

scenario: 团队在评估要不要用云厂商托管的入口层，而不是自己搭一套。
scenario_en: The team is evaluating a cloud-managed entry layer instead of building and operating one itself.
q: 哪些属于云厂商提供的托管 API Gateway / API Management 产品？
q_en: Which options are cloud-provider managed API Gateway or API Management products?
options: AWS API Gateway
Azure API Management
Google Cloud Endpoints
Kong
options_en: AWS API Gateway
Azure API Management
Google Cloud Endpoints
Kong
why: 三大云都有各自的托管入口/API 管理产品；Kong 是一个真实存在的网关，但它是自管开源方案，不是云厂商托管产品。
why_en: AWS API Gateway, Azure API Management, and Google Cloud Endpoints are all managed offerings, while Kong is a real gateway but self-managed, not cloud-managed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 亚马逊的云平台，提供托管 API Gateway 产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS stands for Amazon Web Services, whose managed API Gateway integrates with Lambda and CloudWatch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 谷歌的云平台，Cloud Endpoints 是它的托管网关产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GCP stands for Google Cloud Platform, and Cloud Endpoints is its managed gateway offering.

optionExplanations: AWS API Gateway 是亚马逊云自己的托管入口产品，和 Lambda、CloudWatch 深度集成。
Azure API Management 是微软云的托管服务，OAuth 和策略配置能力较强。
Google Cloud Endpoints 是谷歌云的托管端点服务，和 gRPC、OpenAPI 集成紧密。
Kong 是能打的真实网关，只是要团队自己部署升级，跟云厂商托管完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: AWS API Gateway is Amazon's own managed entry-point product, tightly integrated with Lambda and CloudWatch.
Azure API Management is Microsoft's managed offering, known for strong OAuth and policy configuration.
Google Cloud Endpoints is Google's managed endpoint service, closely integrated with gRPC and OpenAPI.
Kong is a real, capable gateway, but the team has to deploy and upgrade it themselves — a different story from cloud-managed.

scenario: 团队想要更多控制权，愿意自己运维网关而不是用云厂商托管服务。
scenario_en: The team wants more control and is willing to operate the gateway itself instead of using a cloud-managed service.
q: 哪些属于可以自己部署运维的开源 API Gateway？
q_en: Which options are open-source API Gateways the team can deploy and operate itself?
options: Kong
Tyk
Express Gateway
AWS API Gateway
options_en: Kong
Tyk
Express Gateway
AWS API Gateway
why: Kong、Tyk、Express Gateway 都是可以自行部署运维的开源方案；AWS API Gateway 是云厂商托管产品，团队拿不到底层控制权。
why_en: Kong, Tyk, and Express Gateway are open-source options a team can self-host, while AWS API Gateway is a managed cloud product.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种按需查询的 API 查询语言，客户端自己指定要哪些字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets clients request exactly the fields they need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 亚马逊的云平台，提供托管 API Gateway 产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS stands for Amazon Web Services, whose managed API Gateway integrates with Lambda and CloudWatch.

optionExplanations: Kong 基于 NGINX，是团队可以自己部署、按插件扩展的开源网关。
Tyk 用 Go 编写，同样可以自行部署，原生支持 GraphQL。
Express Gateway 是 Node.js 生态的轻量开源网关，也能自己部署运维。
如果团队想要完全自己运维，这一款其实是云厂商托管服务，底层的部署和升级团队都插不上手。
optionExplanations_en: Kong is built on NGINX, an open-source gateway the team can self-host and extend with plugins.
Tyk is written in Go, also self-hostable, with native GraphQL support.
Express Gateway is a lightweight open-source gateway from the Node.js world, also self-deployable.
If the team wants full self-operation, this one is actually a cloud-managed offering — deployment and upgrades stay out of their hands.

scenario: 系统设计面试里，你已经决定用微服务，但主要讨论点其实是 feed、订单或支付等核心业务链路。
scenario_en: In a system design interview, you have chosen microservices, but the main discussion should stay on the core feed, order, or payment flow.
q: 介绍 API Gateway 时最好的处理方式是？
q_en: What is the best way to introduce the API Gateway in the interview?
options: 花十分钟深入讲解每一个 Gateway 插件细节
简要说明路由和基础 middleware，再回核心系统
完全不解释它为什么会出现在设计里
把所有业务逻辑都塞进 Gateway 里处理
options_en: Spend ten minutes explaining every gateway plugin in detail
Briefly cover routing and basic middleware, then return to the core system
Never explain why it even appears in the design
Stuff all business logic into the gateway itself
why: Gateway 是入口层基础设施，重要但通常不是面试主战场；简洁说明 routing + basic middleware 更符合面试节奏。
why_en: In interviews, mention the gateway briefly for routing and middleware, then return to the core system design.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目本身就是设计 API Gateway/API management 平台，才需要深入插件、配置和控制面。
tradeoff: 简洁带过留时间给核心设计 vs 深入插件挤占面试时间
optionExplanations: 面试题不是专门设计网关时，十分钟讲插件细节会挤掉讨论 feed/订单等核心链路的时间。
网关只是入口基础设施时，一句话带过路由和 middleware、再回核心设计最省时间。
设计图里出现了网关却不解释，面试官会怀疑你是不是真的理解自己画的每个组件。
把业务逻辑塞进网关违反了它只做路由和 middleware 的定位，职责放错了地方。
optionExplanations_en: Unless the prompt is literally about designing the gateway, ten minutes on plugin details eats into time the core deserves.
When the gateway is just entry-layer infrastructure, covering routing and middleware in one line and returning to the core saves the most time.
Drawing the gateway without explaining it makes the interviewer doubt you understand every box on your own diagram.
Stuffing business logic into the gateway breaks its routing-and-middleware job, the wrong place for that responsibility.

q: 补全面试中的一句话：
q_en: Complete this concise interview sentence.
text: 引入 API Gateway 时可以说：它负责 {{routing}} 和基础 {{middleware}}，例如 auth/rate limiting，然后不要在入口层细节上过度展开。
why: 这句话同时说清楚核心职责和常见附加能力，也提醒你不要让 Gateway 讨论挤占核心设计时间。
why_en: A concise interview framing is that the gateway handles routing and basic middleware such as authentication and rate limiting.
tradeoff: 一句话带过留时间给核心系统 vs 展开讲挤占面试时间

q: 没有 API Gateway 的微服务客户端通常会出现什么问题？
q_en: What problem do microservice clients usually face without an API Gateway?
options: 客户端要知道多个服务的地址、协议和接口细节，耦合度上升
数据库自动变成强一致多主
所有请求都会天然被限流
客户端完全不需要任何 API contract
options_en: Clients must know every service’s address, protocol, and interface details, and coupling increases
The database automatically becomes strongly-consistent multi-master
Every request is automatically rate limited
Clients no longer need any API contract at all
why: 直接暴露多个微服务会让客户端跟内部拓扑绑定，服务拆分或迁移会一路扩散到客户端；Gateway 能提供稳定的外部 API 表面。
why_en: Without a gateway, clients become coupled to internal service addresses, protocols, and API details.
optionExplanations: 客户端被迫记住每个服务的地址、协议和接口细节，耦合已经外泄到了客户端。
一致性模型和是否存在网关没有因果关系，说法完全不相关。
限流需要显式配置才会生效，不会因为少了网关就凭空出现。
客户端反而更需要明确的 API contract 才知道怎么调用每个服务，说反了方向。
optionExplanations_en: Clients are forced to know every service's address, protocol, and interface details, coupling leaks straight out to them.
The consistency model has no causal link to whether a gateway exists, this is simply unrelated.
Rate limiting only kicks in with explicit configuration, it doesn't appear on its own just because there's no gateway.
Clients need an explicit API contract even more without a gateway to know how to call anything, this has it backwards.

q: 在简单单体应用前硬加 API Gateway 的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of forcing an API Gateway in front of a simple monolith?
options: 增加部署配置复杂度，却没有拓扑隐藏的收益
会自动减少团队所有的运维工作量
会让单体架构自动拆分成微服务
会让数据库查询速度自动变快
options_en: Adds deployment and config complexity without the topology-hiding benefit
Automatically reduces all of the team’s operational workload
Automatically splits the monolith into microservices
Automatically makes database queries faster
why: Gateway 的收益需要多个后端服务或统一入口策略来支撑；简单系统里它只是多一层故障点和配置面。
why_en: Adding a gateway to a simple monolith can add deployment and debugging complexity without a meaningful routing benefit.
optionExplanations: 单体本来只有一个入口，网关的拓扑隐藏收益消失，只剩下多一层配置和故障点。
多加一层组件通常意味着多一层运维，说它会自动减少工作量正好说反了。
架构会不会拆分取决于业务需求，不会因为加了个网关就自动发生。
数据库查询性能要靠具体优化去做，跟前面多了一层网关没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: A monolith already has one entry point, so the topology-hiding benefit disappears, leaving only an extra config layer and failure point.
One more component usually means more ops work, not less, this has it exactly backwards.
Whether the architecture splits depends on business needs, not on whether a gateway got added.
Database query performance needs its own tuning, adding a gateway in front has no causal effect on it.

scenario: 你看到如下 Gateway 路由配置，需要判断 /orders/123 应该走哪个服务。
scenario_en: You see the gateway routing config below and need to decide which service should handle /orders/123.
q: 这份路由配置的作用是什么？
q_en: What does this routing configuration do?
codeSample:
routes:
  - path: /users/*
    service: user-service
    port: 8080
  - path: /orders/*
    service: order-service
    port: 8081
  - path: /payments/*
    service: payment-service
    port: 8082
options: 所有路径请求不分青红皂白，一律都被发到 user-service
/orders/* 请求会被路由到 order-service:8081
这其实是一段数据库表结构 schema 定义
这段配置只用来控制缓存失效策略
options_en: Every path request, no matter what, gets sent to user-service regardless
/orders/* requests are routed to order-service on port 8081
This is actually a database table schema definition
This configuration is only for controlling cache invalidation
why: routing table 把 URL path pattern 映射到后端服务和端口；/orders/123 匹配 /orders/*，所以走 order-service:8081。
why_en: The route table maps the /orders path prefix to the order service on port 8081.
whenOtherWins: 如果路由还依赖 method、header 或 query parameter，就要结合完整规则，不能只看 path。
tradeoff: path 前缀能直接匹配 vs 需要 method/header 才能判断的场景

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识请求资源位置的地址，是 Gateway 路由匹配的主要依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address a gateway’s routing table matches against.

optionExplanations: 配置里明明写了三条不同路径规则，说所有请求都发往 user-service 忽略了这一点。
该请求命中的是 /orders/* 前缀规则，因此配置里会把它转发给订单服务，端口是 8081。
这几行是 path 到 service/port 的映射，跟数据库表结构完全是两种文件。
缓存失效要靠 TTL 或事件字段，这份配置里根本没有，判断错了用途。
optionExplanations_en: The config clearly lists three separate path rules, claiming everything goes to user-service ignores that.
This request matches the /orders/* prefix rule, so the config forwards it to the order-handling service, port 8081.
These lines map a path to a service and port, a completely different kind of file from a database table schema.
Cache invalidation needs a TTL or event field, and neither shows up here, the wrong read on what this file does.

scenario: 团队已经把大部分基础设施放在 AWS 上，正在评估用 AWS 自己的托管网关。
scenario_en: The team already runs most infrastructure on AWS and is evaluating AWS's own managed gateway.
q: AWS API Gateway 的常见能力组合是下面哪一项？
q_en: Which capability set is commonly associated with AWS API Gateway?
options: 只支持 gRPC 这一种协议，完全不提供 REST 或 WebSocket 支持
深度绑定 GCP 云服务生态，完全不支持 AWS Lambda 的集成能力
REST/WebSocket、请求节流、Lambda 集成、CloudWatch 监控
只做流量加密终止，完全不提供节流或监控能力
options_en: Only supports the gRPC protocol, and offers no REST or WebSocket support at all
Deeply tied into GCP's cloud ecosystem, with no AWS Lambda integration capability at all
REST/WebSocket support, throttling, Lambda integration, CloudWatch monitoring
Only handles TLS encryption termination, with no throttling or monitoring capability at all
why: AWS API Gateway 是托管入口产品，和 AWS 生态集成强，常和 Lambda、CloudWatch、API key、节流一起出现。
why_en: AWS API Gateway supports REST and WebSocket APIs, throttling, API keys, Lambda integration, and CloudWatch monitoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 亚马逊的云平台，提供托管 API Gateway 产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS stands for Amazon Web Services, whose managed API Gateway integrates with Lambda and CloudWatch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 谷歌的云平台，Cloud Endpoints 是它的托管网关产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GCP stands for Google Cloud Platform, and Cloud Endpoints is its managed gateway offering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在客户端和服务端之间维持一条长连接、双向推送的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that keeps a long-lived, bidirectional connection open between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 动词和资源路径的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST stands for Representational State Transfer, an API style built on HTTP verbs and resource paths.

optionExplanations: 它明确同时支持 REST 和 WebSocket，说只支持 gRPC 缩窄了协议范围。
它是亚马逊自家产品，天然绑定的是 Lambda/CloudWatch，说成 GCP 生态搞错了归属。
REST/WebSocket、节流、Lambda 集成、CloudWatch 监控正是它和 AWS 生态紧密绑定的体现。
节流和监控都是它的核心能力，说它只做加密终止是把能力范围缩得太窄。
optionExplanations_en: It explicitly supports both REST and WebSocket, limiting it to gRPC only narrows the protocol scope incorrectly.
It's an Amazon product naturally tied to Lambda and CloudWatch, attributing it to GCP gets the ecosystem wrong.
REST/WebSocket support, throttling, Lambda integration, and CloudWatch monitoring show exactly how tightly it binds to AWS.
Throttling and monitoring are core capabilities here, narrowing it to just encryption termination misses most of it.

scenario: 团队想要 NGINX 生态和丰富插件，并且愿意自己运维网关。
scenario_en: The team wants the NGINX ecosystem and rich plugins, and is willing to operate the gateway itself.
q: 哪个开源 Gateway 更贴近这个需求？
q_en: Which open-source gateway best matches this need?
options: Kong
Tyk
Express Gateway
AWS API Gateway
options_en: Kong
Tyk
Express Gateway
AWS API Gateway
why: Kong 基于 NGINX 并以插件生态著称，适合想要自管且保留较强扩展能力的团队。
why_en: Kong is built on NGINX and is known for its broad plugin ecosystem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种按需查询的 API 查询语言，客户端自己指定要哪些字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets clients request exactly the fields they need.

optionExplanations: 需要 NGINX 底座和丰富插件时，Kong 正是这个组合最贴近的选择。
Tyk 的强项是原生 GraphQL 和多数据中心，不是这里要的 NGINX/插件深度。
Express Gateway 轻量好上手，但插件生态比 Kong 单薄，撑不起这个诉求。
AWS API Gateway 是云厂商托管产品，团队根本拿不到自己运维的空间。
optionExplanations_en: When you need an NGINX base with a rich plugin ecosystem, Kong is the closest match.
Tyk's strength is native GraphQL and multi-data-center support, not the NGINX/plugin depth asked for here.
Express Gateway is light and easy but its plugin ecosystem is thinner than Kong's, so it falls short here.
AWS API Gateway is cloud-managed, the team never gets the self-operated control this scenario wants.

scenario: 系统需要原生 GraphQL 支持，并且要在多个数据中心部署入口。
scenario_en: The system needs native GraphQL support and entry points deployed across multiple data centers.
q: 哪个开源 Gateway 更贴近这个需求？
q_en: Which open-source gateway best matches this need?
options: Express Gateway
Tyk
Kong
AWS API Gateway
options_en: Express Gateway
Tyk
Kong
AWS API Gateway
why: Tyk 的特点包括原生 GraphQL 支持、API analytics 和多数据中心能力，正好对应这两个需求。
why_en: Tyk is noted for native GraphQL support, API analytics, and multi-data-center capabilities.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种按需查询的 API 查询语言，客户端自己指定要哪些字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets clients request exactly the fields they need.

optionExplanations: Express Gateway 胜在轻量，但没有覆盖原生 GraphQL 这个硬需求。
需要原生 GraphQL 加多数据中心部署时，Tyk 的这两个强项正好对上。
Kong 的插件生态很强，但那是另一个维度，不是这题要的 GraphQL 能力。
AWS API Gateway 是托管产品，不在"可以自己部署的开源网关"这个候选集合里。
optionExplanations_en: Express Gateway wins on being lightweight, but it doesn't cover the hard requirement of native GraphQL.
When you need native GraphQL plus multi-data-center deployment, Tyk's two headline strengths line up exactly.
Kong's plugin ecosystem is strong, but that's a different dimension than the GraphQL need here.
AWS API Gateway is a managed product, outside the 'self-hostable open source' candidate set this question asks about.

scenario: 团队主要用 Node.js 写微服务，想要轻量、开发者友好的入口层。
scenario_en: The team mainly writes microservices in Node.js and wants a lightweight, developer-friendly entry layer.
q: 哪个开源 Gateway 更贴近这个需求？
q_en: Which open-source gateway best matches this need?
options: Kong
Express Gateway
Tyk
AWS API Gateway
options_en: Kong
Express Gateway
Tyk
AWS API Gateway
why: Express Gateway 是 JavaScript/Node.js based，偏轻量和开发者友好，适合 Node.js 微服务栈中的简单入口管理。
why_en: Express Gateway is a lightweight JavaScript and Node.js gateway that fits Node-based microservices.
optionExplanations: Kong 插件生态强，但要多学一套 NGINX 技术栈，跟团队现有 Node.js 栈不搭。
团队本来就写 Node.js 时，选它就能用熟悉的 JS 工具链管理入口，最省心。
Tyk 的强项是 GraphQL 和多数据中心，跟这里要的轻量、贴近 Node.js 没关系。
AWS API Gateway 是托管产品，不在"开源自管"这个候选集合里。
optionExplanations_en: Kong's plugin ecosystem is strong, but it means learning an NGINX stack that doesn't match the team's Node.js base.
Since the team already writes Node.js, this lightweight option lets them manage the entry with a familiar JS toolchain, the easiest fit.
Tyk's strengths are GraphQL and multi-data-center support, unrelated to the lightweight, Node.js-friendly need here.
AWS API Gateway is a managed product, outside the 'self-managed open source' candidate set.

q: 为什么 API Gateway 通常适合作为横向扩容的组件？
q_en: Why is an API Gateway usually a good component to scale horizontally?
options: 因为它必须把全部用户的会话状态持久化存储在本地磁盘上
因为它会完全替代所有后端服务的职责
因为它只会在离线夜间批量运行
因为它通常不保存业务状态，每个实例可以独立处理请求
options_en: Because it must persist every user's session state to local disk storage
Because it would fully take over every backend service's responsibilities
Because it only runs in scheduled offline batches at night
Because it usually holds no business state, so each instance can handle requests independently
why: stateless 让 Gateway 实例互相可替换，LB 可以自由分流；需要共享的数据应放在外部系统，如配置中心或分布式缓存。
why_en: Gateways usually scale well because they are stateless and each instance can independently handle requests.
optionExplanations: 把会话钉在本地磁盘会破坏实例互换性，反而是扩容的绊脚石。
网关替代后端服务是越权也不现实的设想，跟横向扩容没关系。
网关要 7x24 处理实时流量，说它只在夜间运行不符合实际使用场景。
实例不背业务状态时，谁处理请求都一样，LB 才能自由地往任意实例分流。
optionExplanations_en: Pinning sessions to local disk breaks instance interchangeability, an obstacle to scaling, not a reason for it.
A gateway replacing backend services would be an unrealistic overreach, unrelated to horizontal scaling.
A gateway needs to handle live traffic around the clock, claiming it only runs at night does not match real usage.
With no business state tied to an instance, any instance can handle any request, so the balancer can send traffic anywhere.

scenario: 多个后端服务都需要相同的 JWT 校验和基础限流，团队不想在每个服务里重复实现。
scenario_en: Several backend services need the same JWT validation and basic rate limiting, and the team does not want to reimplement it in every service.
q: 更适合把这些入口策略放在哪里？
q_en: Where should these shared entry policies live?
options: 每个移动端客户端都各自单独实现，服务端完全不管
API Gateway 的 middleware 层
只放在离线数据仓库
只放在某个随机业务服务里
options_en: Each mobile client implements it separately on its own, with the server side not involved at all
The API Gateway’s middleware layer
Only in the offline data warehouse
Only inside one randomly chosen business service
why: 入口统一策略放在 Gateway 能减少重复代码并形成一致的边界控制；业务服务仍可以做更细粒度的授权检查。
why_en: Shared authentication and basic rate limiting belong naturally in gateway middleware to avoid duplicating them per service.
whenOtherWins: 如果授权规则强依赖单个领域模型，业务服务内部仍需要做领域级权限判断。
tradeoff: 网关集中处理省重复代码 vs 领域相关授权仍需服务内部做

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自包含的令牌格式，把身份和权限声明编码进去，放在请求头里传递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JWT stands for JSON Web Token, a self-contained token that encodes identity claims and travels in the request header.

optionExplanations: 校验逻辑放在客户端等于把安全边界交给了不可信的一方，很容易被绕过。
多个服务要共享同一套 JWT 校验和限流时，放在网关的 middleware 层能一次实现、处处生效。
离线数据仓库不面对同步入口流量，起不到拦截实时请求的作用。
塞进某一个业务服务只保护了那一个服务，其余服务依旧暴露在外。
optionExplanations_en: Putting the check on the client hands the security boundary to an untrusted party, trivially bypassed.
When several services need the same JWT validation and rate limiting, the gateway's middleware layer implements it once and it applies everywhere.
An offline data warehouse never sees synchronous entry traffic, so it can't intercept live requests.
Placing it inside one business service only protects that service, the rest stay exposed.

q: Gateway 与 service discovery 集成的意义是什么？
q_en: Why should a gateway integrate with service discovery?
options: 让 Gateway 找到健康实例，不写死单个地址
让用户绕过网关，直接连接到后端数据库内部
让网关变成一个离线模型训练器
让每个请求都必须先失败重试一次
options_en: Letting the gateway find healthy instances instead of a hardcoded address
Letting users bypass the gateway and connect straight into the backend database internals
Turning the gateway into an offline model trainer
Forcing every request to fail once before it can retry
why: 当后端服务实例扩缩容或替换时，Gateway 需要知道当前可用实例集合；服务发现避免把易变地址硬编码进路由配置。
why_en: Service discovery lets a gateway route to healthy backend instances without hardcoding fixed addresses.
tradeoff: 动态发现健康实例 vs 硬编码地址简单但脆弱
optionExplanations: 服务实例会扩缩容或替换时，动态发现让网关始终转发到健康实例，不必硬编码地址。
绕开网关直连数据库暴露了内部细节，也削弱了入口层本该有的控制。
离线训练和实时请求路由是完全不同的两套系统，服务发现不做这件事。
服务发现是找可用实例，不是逼每个请求先失败一次再重试，机制搞混了。
optionExplanations_en: As instances scale or get replaced, dynamic discovery keeps the gateway forwarding to healthy ones instead of a hardcoded address.
Bypassing the gateway straight to the database exposes internals and weakens the entry-layer control it's meant to provide.
Offline training and live request routing are two entirely different systems, discovery doesn't do this.
Discovery is about finding available instances, not forcing every request to fail once before retrying, wrong mechanism.

q: API Gateway 设置 response timeout 的作用是什么？
q_en: What is the purpose of setting a response timeout at the API Gateway?
options: 保证所有后端永远不会变慢
让缓存永远不过期
避免慢后端请求无限占用入口资源，并给客户端明确失败
把同步的 API 自动转变成离线 job 任务
options_en: Guaranteeing backends will never slow down
Making the cache never lapse
Preventing slow backend calls from tying up gateway resources indefinitely, and giving clients a clear failure
Automatically turning a synchronous API into an offline job task
why: timeout 是入口层保护机制，防止慢请求耗尽连接和线程；它不能修复后端性能问题，但能限制故障扩散。
why_en: Gateway timeouts prevent slow backend calls from tying up entry-point resources indefinitely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，过期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL stands for Time To Live, the duration a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 后端还是可能变慢，超时只是限制影响范围，改变不了后端本身的性能。
缓存过期靠 TTL 字段，跟入口层的 response timeout 是两个不同机制。
后端变慢时，超时给连接和线程占用设了上限，还能立刻给客户端一个明确失败。
协议模式的转换要显式设计，不会因为设了超时就自动从同步变成异步。
optionExplanations_en: The backend can still slow down, a timeout only caps the blast radius, it doesn't change backend performance itself.
Cache lapsing runs on a TTL field, a separate mechanism from a gateway's response timeout.
When a backend slows down, a timeout caps how long connections and threads stay tied up, and gives a clear failure right away.
Turning a sync call into an offline job needs explicit design, a timeout alone doesn't do that automatically.

q: 为什么 API Gateway 是记录入口流量日志和基础指标的好位置？
q_en: Why is the API Gateway a good place to log entry traffic and basic metrics?
options: 它能看到所有外部请求的统一入口视角
它能看到用户手机上的所有本地文件
它只处理数据库内部 WAL
它会替代所有 observability 系统
options_en: It sees every external request from one unified entry point
It can see every local file on a user’s phone
It only handles the database’s internal WAL
It replaces the entire observability system
why: Gateway 位于客户端和服务之间，天然能记录 request path、status、latency、rate limit 命中等入口指标；更深的业务指标仍靠服务和观测平台补充。
why_en: The gateway is a good place for entry traffic logs because it sees all client-facing requests in one layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库先写日志再落盘的持久化机制，和 Gateway 入口日志是两回事。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WAL stands for Write-Ahead Log, a database durability mechanism unrelated to gateway request logging.

optionExplanations: 所有外部请求都经过这一层，路径、状态码、延迟这些入口指标天然能在这统一采集。
网关看不到客户端本地设备上的文件，这已经越出了它能触达的范围。
WAL 是数据库自己的持久化机制，跟网关记录入口流量完全是两回事。
网关只是可观测性拼图的一块，业务指标仍要靠服务和观测平台补上，说它能替代全部夸大了。
optionExplanations_en: Every external request passes through this one layer, so path, status code, and latency are naturally easy to collect here.
The gateway has no way to reach files on a user's local device, that's outside what it can ever see.
WAL is the database's own durability mechanism, unrelated to a gateway logging entry traffic.
The gateway is only one piece of observability, business metrics still need services and a monitoring platform, so calling it a full replacement overstates it.

q: 把"是否引入 API Gateway"的决策链按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the decision chain for whether to introduce an API Gateway in order.
steps: 如果只是简单 monolith，Gateway 可能是额外复杂度
客户端不应耦合到每个内部服务地址和协议
引入 Gateway 作为统一入口，处理路由和基础 middleware
系统是微服务架构，有多个后端服务
Gateway 保持 stateless，并放在 LB 后水平扩容
why: 先识别微服务和客户端耦合问题，再引入 Gateway 并说明扩展方式，最后点出它不适用的边界；这个链条比画一个盒子更有说服力。
why_en: The decision starts with microservices and client coupling, then adds a stateless gateway for routing and middleware while noting when it is overkill.
tradeoff: 微服务需要统一入口 vs 简单单体多背一层复杂度
